_about: Each month's sign tied to its book of the Gaiad (Emma, 2026-11-10: "We can connect the themes to the signs somehow even in big stretches of reinterpretation"; she took all thirteen, for each book's opening, the month pages and the wiki's month articles). Used by build.py (month pages) and scripts/build_book.py (book openings). Draft history: inochi-no-michikyo research/signs-and-books.md.

sagittarius.text: The heart of our galaxy lies in Sagittarius: the great dark centre the astronomers call Sagittarius A*. The Archer aims at it, and the Book of the Yarn begins there, with the thread spun out from the centre of all things.

capricorn.text: Capricorn is the Sea-Goat, half fish and half climber. So is the Book of Kingdoms: life born in the sea, building its first kingdoms there, and already turning toward the heights.

aquarius.text: Aquarius is the Water-Bearer, and the water it bears is the sea inside the egg: in the Book of Janus life leaves the water by carrying it along. Janus has two faces, and this is the threshold they look across, the water behind and the land ahead.

pisces.text: Pisces is the two Fishes. One is the ichthyosaur, the fish-lizard, going back into the sea; the other is the ichthys, the fish of Easter. The Book of Pascha is a book of death and rising: the Great Dying, and the world that came back after it.

aries.text: Aries is the Ram, the old first sign of the year. The Book of Stone is humanity's beginning, and it ends among the first farmers, who kept the sheep among the first of all their herds.

taurus.text: Taurus is the Bull, and the age the astrologers call the Age of Taurus is roughly the Bronze Age itself. It was an age of bulls: the Apis of Egypt, the Bull of Heaven that Gilgamesh fought, the bull-leapers of Crete.

gemini.text: Gemini is the Twins, and the Book of Iron is full of them: Rome and Han, twin empires at the two ends of the world; Romulus and Remus; Castor and Pollux, whose temple stood in the Roman Forum; and the twin spirits of Zarathustra's hymns.

cancer.text: Cancer is the Crab, which carries its house on its back and goes sideways. So Rome went on in the Book of Romans: its shell carried by others, by Byzantium and by a Holy Roman Empire, and by everyone who called themselves Roman.

leo.text: Leo is the Lion, and Leo is Lehi. The Lion's month is the high summer, ruled by the sun, when the ancestors come home; and the Lion is the line handed down, from the fathers and mothers to their children.

virgo.text: Virgo is the Virgin, who holds an ear of wheat. In the Book of Confluence she is the Virgin of Guadalupe, in whom the old world of Mexico and the new faith met in 1531, and the wheat in her hand is the harvest of the world crossing the oceans.

libra.text: Libra is the Scales: reason weighing, justice, the balance of powers. Libra begins at the autumn equinox, and so did the French Republican calendar, on the 22nd of September 1792. The Gaian calendar keeps the equinox, and keeps the week.

scorpio.text: Scorpio is the Scorpion, and its sting is the twentieth century's: the bomb and the venom of war. It is the season of the dead, from Halloween and the Day of the Dead to Remembrance Day on the 11th of November, and the Book of Hours counts the hours of that century.

ophiuchus.text: Ophiuchus is the Serpent-Bearer, Asclepius, the healer who was struck down for raising the dead. It is the thirteenth sign, the one the usual zodiac leaves out, put back. The Book of Omega is its book: healing, the sleepers in the cold, and the dead raised.
